findings.reason: the deliverable needs one clause saying the digest identity is opted into by the resource reader's head parse only, otherwise a literal implementation spends a file read per memoized call on the read path and works against §50's and §56's latency measures.
findings.text: §57's deliverable ("`memoized` learns a content-digest identity, so identical content at two paths parses once") does not scope the new key, and `memoized` today keys on a stat signature (`reckon/file_memo.py:270-290`) that every read-path caller relies on: `reckon/roadmap.py:212/252/480/519/1658`, `reckon/section` reads in `reckon/_plan_html.py:1544/1563/2359` and `reckon/serve.py:728/1079` all memoize with `variant=None`, so a content digest made the default key forces a full file read on every one of those calls in place of a single `os.stat` — on the very roadmap recompute that §50 and §56 exist to bring inside the deadline on slow GPFS — while the section's done-when (`grep` zero, three tests pass, one new parse-count test) is satisfied either way and so cannot catch the choice
